agentCan: Prepare every registration value and draft the minimal delegated-permission list with justifications
Implement the authorization-code flow, refresh handling, and a dedicated admin-consent connect view for customer tenants
Draft the publisher-verification and admin-onboarding materials

approval.cost: Free (Microsoft charges nothing for publisher verification; no license required)
approval.trigger: Microsoft runs no review of your app: register and you can request consent immediately. The real approval is distributed: every customer tenant's admin must grant consent for admin-restricted or application permissions (and some tenants block user consent entirely). Separately, Microsoft Publisher Verification (identity check, blue verified badge) is optional on paper but near-mandatory for B2B: since Nov 2020, where risk-based step-up consent is enabled, users cannot consent to most non-verified multitenant apps.
approval.wait: None from Microsoft. Publisher verification is stated as 'verified in minutes' once partner prerequisites are met; partner-program enrollment duration is not stated

blockers.detail: Consent is granted tenant by tenant; there is no global approval. If your app requests admin-restricted permissions (User.Read.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, Group.Read.All) or any application permission, a normal user's click fails and that tenant's admin must approve via the admin consent endpoint. This repeats for every new customer, forever.
blockers.howToClear: Build an admin-facing connect flow (send the admin to login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0/adminconsent) and treat admin onboarding as part of your sales motion, not an error case.
blockers.title: Per-tenant admin consent is the real approval

blockers.detail: Without publisher verification, the consent screen warns the app 'was created by an unverified publisher and that the app is risky', and many tenants hard-block consent to unverified multitenant apps outright. Verification requires a Microsoft partner (AI Cloud Partner Program, formerly MPN) account with completed identity verification, a PartnerID associated to the app, and a publisher domain that is not *.onmicrosoft.com.
blockers.howToClear: Complete partner enrollment and publisher verification before selling to enterprises; budget the enrollment as the one real schedule unknown on your side.
blockers.title: Unverified-publisher warning (and often a hard block)

blockers.detail: Delegated Mail.Read reads the consenting user's mail. Application Mail.Read reads EVERY mailbox in the tenant, always requires admin consent, and gets heavy scrutiny from customer admins. Asking for application permissions 'just in case' is the most common self-inflicted blocker.
blockers.howToClear: Default to delegated permissions that act as the signed-in user; use application permissions only for genuine daemon scenarios.
blockers.title: The application-permissions trap

tested: Read-only verification: registration flavors, permission model, admin-consent mechanics, and publisher-verification requirements were checked against current learn.microsoft.com pages (no app registered, nothing submitted). Several consent-framework pages returned 403 to the reader and are flagged below rather than asserted.
unverified: Exact tenant user-consent policy menu and the admin consent request workflow: the enterprise-apps consent pages returned 403 in this research pass; the existence of admin-configured consent policies keyed on publisher verification is stated in the publisher-verification overview.
Whether customer Conditional Access policies (MFA, compliant device, location) block an agent's tokens after consent: known platform behavior, but no Conditional Access doc was opened in this pass.
Partner-program (CPP/MPN) enrollment and identity-verification duration: not stated in the docs read.
Microsoft 365 Publisher Attestation / App Certification timelines (optional deeper trust programs): not verified in this pass.
The 'no Microsoft review' finding is an absence in the docs reviewed (no review step is described), not a Microsoft statement that none exists.

alternatives: Single-tenant registration (only your own org's users; wrong for a product)
Application permissions (app acts as itself with no user; daemon services only, always admin-consented)
flavor.recommended: App registration in Microsoft Entra ID, 'Multiple Entra ID tenants' supported account types, delegated permissions
flavor.why: An app registration is the OAuth app object; registering creates the Application (client) ID, and a service principal is instantiated in each tenant that consents. Multitenant is Microsoft's own recommendation for SaaS apps serving multiple organizations. Delegated permissions make the app act on behalf of the signed-in user, which is the correct model for a user-connected agent (delegated Mail.Read, Mail.Send, Calendars.Read).

humanMust: Hold an Azure account with at least the Application Developer role and create the registration
Decide account types and the delegated permission set
Complete partner-program enrollment and publisher verification (roles + MFA required)
Each customer's tenant admin grants consent on their side
name: Outlook (Microsoft 365)
nuances: The app registration cannot be moved between tenants once created; registering in the wrong tenant (or under a personal account, which also cannot be publisher verified) means starting over.
Request offline_access to receive refresh tokens; access tokens last about 1 hour, refresh tokens typically 90 days.
App registrations are hidden from users by default; set 'Visible to users? = Yes' on the Enterprise apps Properties page when ready.
Redirect URIs are per-platform (web, SPA, mobile/desktop) and the runtime redirect_uri must exactly match a registered one.
Publisher verification is not supported in national cloud tenants.
prerequisites: An Azure account with an active subscription and at least the Application Developer role
A workforce tenant (the default directory is fine)
A verified custom domain for the publisher domain (needed for publisher verification)
For publisher verification: a Microsoft partner account with completed identity verification

steps.detail: Entra admin center > App registrations > New registration: name the app, choose Supported account types = 'Multiple Entra ID tenants' (add personal Microsoft accounts only for a genuine consumer product), Register. Record the Application (client) ID from the Overview page.
steps.title: Register the app (multitenant)

steps.detail: Authentication blade: add redirect URIs for each platform you ship (web, SPA, mobile/desktop). The runtime redirect_uri must exactly match a registered URI. Under Certificates & secrets, add a client secret or certificate (required for confidential web clients).
steps.title: Add redirect URIs and a credential

steps.detail: API permissions blade: add Microsoft Graph DELEGATED permissions only what you need (e.g. Mail.Read, Mail.Send, Calendars.Read, User.Read is auto-assigned). Microsoft instructs least privilege explicitly: broad sets erode admin trust and consent rates. Avoid admin-restricted scopes unless the feature truly needs them.
steps.title: Configure minimal delegated permissions

steps.detail: Authorization code flow against login.microsoftonline.com; include offline_access for refresh tokens (access ~1 hr, refresh typically 90 days). Build a dedicated admin connect view that sends a customer's tenant admin to the admin consent endpoint (login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/v2.0/adminconsent) so the whole tenant is approved in one act; success returns admin_consent=True and creates your service principal in their tenant.
steps.title: Implement the flow, including an admin-consent path

steps.detail: Associate your partner account's PartnerID (global account) with the app registration, ensure the publisher domain is a verified custom domain (not *.onmicrosoft.com), and complete verification (initiator needs Entra app-admin role + Partner Center admin role + MFA sign-in). Stated: free, and 'verified in minutes' once prerequisites are met. Skipping this leaves your consent screen with the unverified-publisher warning.
steps.time: Minutes if partner-ready; partner enrollment duration unstated
steps.title: Get publisher verified

tagline: No Microsoft review queue exists; you can register and request consent the same day. The approvals that matter are per-customer: each tenant's admin consents separately, and an unverified publisher badge quietly kills B2B conversions.

time.active: One portal session for registration and configuration + ~half a day of flow code
time.total: Same day to a connectable app; real-world enterprise adoption time is dominated by each customer's admin consent and your partner enrollment
